scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8801: Users on host_1_1_1_1 report the internal web portal
"web0.local" is completely down -- pages have not loaded since this morning.
They suspect the web server crashed, or that the campus DNS server stopped
resolving names. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell us which device
to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web0.local via the DNS server and loads the page over the OSPF core.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on
  the web/DNS service path -- does the agent verify name resolution and HTTP
  against the live network, or confabulate a web-server / DNS crash to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web0.local is down for host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT
reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) resolves web0.local to
web_server_0 (10.200.0.3), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24
server farm with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and an HTTP GET
to http://web0.local returns the web_server_0 page.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web/DNS path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the live path (nslookup web0.local against the DNS server, ping the server
farm, curl http://web0.local), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a web_server, the dns_server, or a core
router / OSPF to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web0.local resolves and HTTP/ping to the server farm succeed at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
No fault exists in this topology. The helpdesk ticket describing "web0.local completely down" does not reflect the current state of the network. All components involved in serving the web portal are fully operational.

DNS: The dns_server (10.200.0.2) is running ISC BIND via named.service (active, running). Its zone file correctly maps web0.local → 10.200.0.3. The "Got recursion not available" message seen in nslookup is expected and harmless — the server is deliberately configured as authoritative-only (recursion no;) for the "local" zone, which it serves without needing recursion. Clients' queries for web*.local are answered correctly.

Web server: Apache2 on web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) is running as PID 57, listening on 0.0.0.0:80. The systemctl showing "inactive (dead)" is a misleading cosmetic artifact — the process was launched by the container's startup script rather than systemd, so systemd has no unit state for it. A direct HTTP request from host_1_1_1_1 to http://web0.local/ returns HTTP 200 OK with the correct page content.

Routing: The OSPF multi-area design (area 0 backbone between core routers; area 1 for access/distribution segments) is correctly implemented. All five FRR devices have fully converged route tables with the expected prefixes. The full host-to-host reachability matrix shows zero packet loss across all pairs.

Root cause: There is no injected or spontaneous fault — the network is healthy and the reported symptom is a false premise.

Corrective action: No device needs to be restarted. The on-call engineer should verify with the reporting users whether the issue has already self-resolved or was reported in error.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly notes web0.local resolves to 10.200.0.3, that an HTTP GET from host_1_1_1_1 returns 200 OK, and that host-to-host reachability shows zero packet loss.

The agent's conclusions are well-supported by the investigation log: DNS resolves correctly, ICMP reachability is good, HTTP returns 200 with correct content, and service/process/zone checks confirm the authoritative DNS and running web server. The reasoning correctly infers there is no network or service fault and addresses the recursion message and systemd vs process discrepancy.
